subject: english
title: How Sea Otters Stay Warm
parent_tip: Read the article together first. Then ask: what surprised you?

items.ask: According to paragraph 1, what keeps most sea mammals warm?
choices: a thick layer of fat called blubber
a coat of very long and oily fur
the warm water near the coast

items.ask: What does the short, soft underfur do?
choices: It helps the otter crack open shells.
It keeps the otter from sinking too deep.
It traps a layer of air next to the skin.

items.ask: Why do sea otters need to eat so much food every day?
choices: Staying warm takes a lot of energy.
They cannot find food in winter.

items.ask: Why does a sea otter spend hours grooming? Use a detail from paragraph 3.
Copy the sentence from paragraph 5 that tells why an otter wraps itself in kelp.

answer_key: 1. A (a thick layer of fat called blubber)
2. C (It traps a layer of air next to the skin.)
3. B (Staying warm takes a lot of energy.)
4. Sample: A sea otter grooms because its coat only works when it is clean. A dirty, matted coat would let cold water reach the skin.
5. Sample: The kelp keeps the sleeping otter from drifting away while it floats.
